title: Integration (Software Integration)
seoTitle: What Is Software Integration? A Guide for Business Owners
seoDescription: Software integration connects your business systems so data moves automatically. Types, costs, timelines and how to decide between connectors and custom builds.
summary: Software integration is the work of connecting separate business systems, such as accounting, CRM, e-commerce and WhatsApp, so information moves between them automatically and correctly. It removes re-typing, speeds up processes and gives one reliable version of the numbers.

dataPoints.label: Common SME pairs
dataPoints.value: Tally with Shopify or Razorpay, CRM with WhatsApp, website forms with CRM, ERP with e-invoicing

dataPoints.label: Approaches
dataPoints.value: Ready-made connectors, no-code tools (Zapier, Make, n8n), or custom code

dataPoints.label: Typical timeline
dataPoints.value: Days for a connector; 2–8 weeks for a custom integration

dataPoints.label: Ongoing need
dataPoints.value: Monitoring, error alerts and updates when either system changes

body:
## Three ways to integrate

1. **Ready-made connectors**: fast and inexpensive for standard needs, limited when your rules are specific.
2. **No-code automation tools**: flexible for simple, low-volume flows. See [n8n, Make or custom code](/blog/workflow-automation-with-n8n-make-or-custom-code-how-to-choose).
3. **Custom integration**: built around your business rules, with proper error handling and logs. Best for critical, high-volume flows.

## What makes an integration reliable

- Clear rules for what moves, in which direction, and which system is the source of truth.
- Handling for failures: retries, alerts, and a way to fix and re-send records.
- Monitoring, so a silent failure does not go unnoticed for weeks.

Browse our [integrations guides](/integrations) for specific tool pairs.

faqs.a: Mostly, but budget for maintenance: APIs change, credentials expire and business rules evolve.

faqs.q: How do I know if I need integration?
faqs.a: If staff re-type the same data into two systems every day, or reports disagree between systems, integration usually pays back quickly.
